subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should OpenClaw expose ordinary plugin runtime access to plugin-registered Gateway methods, and what authorization/API shape should carry caller identity?
rationale: The implementation would change the public Plugin SDK and Gateway authorization boundary, so automation cannot safely choose between raw dispatch, allowlisted calls, or typed service/capability contracts.

options.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
options.body: Expose only approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep HTTP-route dispatch only
options.body: Decline ordinary plugin-to-plugin Gateway calls and require plugins to use existing HTTP route or capability seams.

options.title: Expose raw Gateway dispatch
options.body: Add a generic method-string caller and accept the larger security and compatibility surface as a maintainer-owned product decision.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
recommendation.body: Expose only approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest current history match for Gateway/plugin method policy and public SDK boundary decisions.
